statusDetail: Coverage-complete representative audit of homepage, section, article, search, and error templates.

page.notes: Turkish public news site with a PWA manifest/service worker and extensive ad/analytics integrations.

checkOutcomes.method: Emulated prefers-color-scheme: dark screenshot plus CSS/computed-style probe
checkOutcomes.evidence: The dark-condition screenshot is byte-identical to the light screenshot, computed color-scheme is normal, and the CSS probe found no prefers-color-scheme, color-scheme, or light-dark() support.
Under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, the probe matched the preference and found zero active animations; no auto-advance or essential motion appeared in the captured state.

checkOutcomes.method: CSS feature probe plus Lighthouse contrast audit
checkOutcomes.evidence: The CSS probe found no prefers-contrast or forced-colors adaptation, while Lighthouse found essential market values with contrast as low as 2.5:1.

checkOutcomes.method: CSS/DOM feature probe across MPA routes
checkOutcomes.evidence: The CSS/DOM probe found no View Transition declarations or startViewTransition usage on this multi-page news experience; route changes are abrupt full-document swaps.

checkOutcomes.method: Repeated scroll interaction plus CSS/animation probe
checkOutcomes.evidence: Repeated full-page scrolling showed no scroll-linked animation, parallax, or reveal effect to implement; the CSS probe found no scroll timeline and no active animations.

checkOutcomes.method: DOM interaction inventory and mobile screenshots
checkOutcomes.evidence: The representative news, section, search, and article surfaces expose conventional links and vertical scrolling, with no custom swipe/pointer gesture that fights native behavior.

checkOutcomes.method: Computed header style, repeated scroll interaction, and mobile layout
checkOutcomes.evidence: The header is fixed at 52px but the CSS probe found no scroll-state container query or progress behavior; it remains static through a 25,714px mobile page.
No authored tooltip, transient popover, or edge-positioned menu was present on the representative content paths; the consent UI is third-party modal UI rather than an anchored disclosure.
checkOutcomes.reason: No authored tooltip, transient popover, or edge-positioned menu was present on the representative content paths; the consent UI is third-party modal UI rather than an anchored disclosure.

checkOutcomes.evidence: The multi-page navigation provides no transition, focus cue, progress marker, or highlight when moving among dense listing and article templates.
Every first-load screenshot is covered by a viewport-dominating consent wall before any news can be read, on desktop and mobile.

checkOutcomes.method: DOM semantic inventory and article heading probe
checkOutcomes.evidence: The rendered DOM contains no dialog or popover element even though a modal consent surface is shown and adds multiple H1 elements.

checkOutcomes.method: Desktop/mobile screenshots and computed header dimensions
checkOutcomes.evidence: Behind the consent layer, the captured templates use a compact 52px header and content-led card/article layouts rather than a persistent application frame.
At 360x800 the homepage and section both report scrollWidth 360, horizontalOverflowPx 0, and a viewport meta tag.
The CSS probe found no @container or container-type usage across a page with reusable cards and finance/news modules.
Programmatically focused navigation, search, and account controls consistently computed outline-style:none with no box-shadow focus indicator.
The page title and underlying content identify the news purpose, but the entire initial viewport is replaced by consent copy and competing consent controls.
Reading the homepage, opening an article, browsing a section, and viewing search results all begin with the same blocking consent wall, adding a mandatory detour before the core reading flow.
The invalid-route test shows an explicit “500 - Sunucu Hatası” state, explanatory text, and an “ANASAYFAYA DÖN” recovery action.
Lighthouse measured LCP 18.3s and performance 0.56; the trace also measured LCP 3.89s and TBT 983.8ms, both showing a poor load under the captured conditions.
The mobile layout observer measured CLS 0.026 on home and 0.024 on the section, both within the good range, and only two small shifts on home.
The trace found three long tasks, a 948.6ms longest task, and 983.8ms total blocking time; Lighthouse reported 4.1s main-thread work and 2.2s JS execution.

checkOutcomes.method: HAR summary confirmed against script attributes plus Lighthouse
checkOutcomes.evidence: The load made 216 requests and transferred 5.64MB; 139 image requests, 8 fonts (798KB), parser-inserted styles/scripts, redirects, and a network dependency warning delay content.

checkOutcomes.method: HAR summary and live script inventory
checkOutcomes.evidence: 29 scripts transferred 1.47MB; multiple GTM/gtag, ad bidding, analytics, and duplicate GPT loads dominate the script inventory and third-party bytes.

checkOutcomes.method: Lighthouse accessibility details, form inventory, and image audit
checkOutcomes.evidence: Lighthouse failed link-name and accessibility-tree audits; the search input has no label or aria-label, and the image audit found five missing alt attributes.
Lighthouse found market values at 2.5:1 and 4.05:1 against white, below the 4.5:1 minimum for 14px normal text.

checkOutcomes.method: Heading and focus probe across home/article
checkOutcomes.evidence: The homepage probe found no H1 among its first 30 headings and focused controls had no visible outline; the article gains several consent-system H1s in addition to its article H1.

checkOutcomes.method: Article DOM probe and mobile screenshot
checkOutcomes.evidence: Article body copy is exposed as real text with a clear H1 and paragraph flow; mobile screenshots show reflow rather than clipped columns.

checkOutcomes.method: Viewport/media probe and mobile layout metrics
checkOutcomes.evidence: The viewport allows scaling (no maximum-scale/user-scalable=no), mobile layouts have no overflow, and no essential video/audio requiring captions was present in the sampled templates.
Lighthouse explicitly failed “Browser errors were logged to the console.”
The document has doctype and charset, but the image audit found 56 images without srcset, 57 legacy-format images, two missing dimensions, and five missing alt values.

checkOutcomes.method: Lighthouse best-practices details and run output
checkOutcomes.evidence: Lighthouse found a deprecated API, Inspector issues, five BFCache failure reasons, and a missing source-map mapping warning during the run.
Home and article expose specific titles and meta descriptions in both rendered and raw HTML.
Internal navigation uses real same-origin hrefs, viewport metadata is present, and robots.txt allows the public site and article URLs.

checkOutcomes.method: Metadata probes, discoverability status, and robots.txt
checkOutcomes.evidence: Home and article return 200, expose matching canonical URLs, robots allows them, and robots.txt names a Google News sitemap.
The article contains NewsArticle JSON-LD and complete Open Graph title, description, URL, and 1200x800 image metadata matching visible content.
HTTPS is used, but CSP, HSTS, X-Content-Type-Options, framing protection, Referrer-Policy, and Permissions-Policy are all absent; 16 observed cookies were flagged as not Secure.
The page contacted 31 third-party origins; 156 third-party requests transferred 4.76MB and known Google/DoubleClick trackers plus Yandex/Gemius/ad-tech requests loaded on first visit.
No notification/geolocation prompt appeared on load and the representative public reading journey requires no authentication; secrets scanning found no exposed credential.
The response has no HSTS, clickjacking defense, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy, or CSP frame-ancestors fallback.
Raw HTML retained 94% of homepage and 78% of article content; neither page is a JS shell, and article title/H1/description survive without JavaScript.

checkOutcomes.method: Discoverability, HAR error signals, and representative screenshots
checkOutcomes.evidence: Core content is server-rendered, standard links survive, and the tested templates remained rendered through delayed third-party failures without a blank shell.
The page links a valid standalone manifest with icons, shortcuts, start_url and scope, and serviceWorker is available/used by the site.
A deliberately unknown URL is labeled and rendered as “500 - Sunucu Hatası” rather than a correct 404, making a missing page look like a transient server outage despite offering a home link.
html lang is tr, Turkish reading direction correctly defaults to LTR, and the CSS probe found logical inline properties in use.

checkOutcomes.method: Article semantic time probe and Lighthouse node labels
checkOutcomes.evidence: Article dates are human-readable in Turkish numeric convention and pair with machine-readable datetime values; finance values use Turkish decimal commas.
Primary publication/update time elements include explicit +03:00 offsets, making the instant unambiguous.
Tracking and advertising requests are already present in the first-load HAR while the consent wall asks for a decision; the blocking wall obscures content on every sampled route.
No authored data-entry form with validation was part of the representative public reading flow; the only visible text form is search.
checkOutcomes.reason: No authored data-entry form with validation was part of the representative public reading flow; the only visible text form is search.

checkOutcomes.evidence: The search input has autocomplete="off" and no associated label or aria-label, obstructing input assistance and accessible identification.
No checkout, subscription purchase, sensitive account-management, or authenticated action was part of this public news-reading audit; member login was not required for the core task.
checkOutcomes.reason: No checkout, subscription purchase, sensitive account-management, or authenticated action was part of this public news-reading audit; member login was not required for the core task.

checkOutcomes.evidence: Images transferred 3.25MB across 139 requests; 57 use legacy formats and 56 lack responsive srcset, while Lighthouse estimates 198KiB image savings.
The initial page performs 216 requests and 4.1s of main-thread work, including analytics, ad auction, cookie-sync redirects, and background tracking before the user reaches content.
Third parties account for 156 requests and 4.76MB, including multiple ad/analytics stacks; this is disproportionate for a primarily text-and-image news listing.
For this read-only news surface, no transactional WebMCP tool is needed; article capabilities are exposed through crawlable server-rendered text and NewsArticle JSON-LD rather than opaque client UI.
The site offers no summarisation or language-model feature whose inference placement can be judged; adding AI is an optional product decision, not a quality requirement.
checkOutcomes.reason: The site offers no summarisation or language-model feature whose inference placement can be judged; adding AI is an optional product decision, not a quality requirement.

checkOutcomes.evidence: After ten full-page scroll down/up cycles, heap self-size was 40.0MB versus a 38.6MB fresh baseline (+3.8%); closures were effectively flat (35,074 to 35,090), with no evidence of unbounded retained growth in this bounded test.
The fresh loaded homepage heap summary reports 38.6MB self-size; this is proportionate to the ad- and image-heavy page and did not balloon in the repeated-scroll sample.

checkOutcomes.method: Before/after heap constructor and node-type comparison
checkOutcomes.evidence: The top constructors contain no Detached* population; closures changed by only 16 and arrays decreased after repeated scrolling, providing no accumulation signal in this test.

paths.description: Homepage and primary news-discovery entry point; tested desktop, mobile, dark/reduced-motion, performance, network, privacy, accessibility and memory.
Representative NewsArticle detail template, including metadata, reading content and no-JS visibility.
Search results journey for “ekonomi”, representing the primary query flow.
Unknown route used to inspect HTTP/error recovery behavior.

findings.summary: Light-only presentation ignores dark preference
findings.evidence: The dark-condition screenshot is byte-identical to the light screenshot, computed color-scheme is normal, and the CSS probe found no prefers-color-scheme, color-scheme, or light-dark() support.
findings.suggestedFix: Add color-scheme: light dark and theme surfaces with prefers-color-scheme or light-dark().

findings.summary: No high-contrast adaptation
findings.evidence: The CSS probe found no prefers-contrast or forced-colors adaptation, while Lighthouse found essential market values with contrast as low as 2.5:1.
findings.suggestedFix: Add forced-colors/prefers-contrast rules and preserve visible control/text boundaries.

findings.summary: Route changes are abrupt
findings.evidence: The CSS/DOM probe found no View Transition declarations or startViewTransition usage on this multi-page news experience; route changes are abrupt full-document swaps.
findings.suggestedFix: Enable cross-document View Transitions with a conservative fallback and reduced-motion handling.

findings.summary: Long-page chrome does not respond to scroll state
findings.evidence: The header is fixed at 52px but the CSS probe found no scroll-state container query or progress behavior; it remains static through a 25,714px mobile page.
findings.suggestedFix: Use CSS scroll-state queries or a lightweight progress affordance for the long feed.

findings.summary: Navigation changes lack attention cues
findings.evidence: The multi-page navigation provides no transition, focus cue, progress marker, or highlight when moving among dense listing and article templates.
findings.suggestedFix: Preserve focus and add directional or highlight cues around route/in-page navigation.

findings.summary: Consent wall obscures all content on load
findings.evidence: Every first-load screenshot is covered by a viewport-dominating consent wall before any news can be read, on desktop and mobile.
findings.suggestedFix: Replace the full-content interruption with a compact, non-blocking, equally clear consent surface; keep refusal immediately available.

findings.summary: Modal consent UI lacks authored dialog semantics
findings.evidence: The rendered DOM contains no dialog or popover element even though a modal consent surface is shown and adds multiple H1 elements.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a correctly labelled dialog only when modality is essential, with platform focus management and dismissal.

findings.summary: Reusable modules rely only on viewport responsiveness
findings.evidence: The CSS probe found no @container or container-type usage across a page with reusable cards and finance/news modules.
findings.suggestedFix: Adopt container queries for cards/modules reused across column widths.

findings.summary: Keyboard focus is not visible
findings.evidence: Programmatically focused navigation, search, and account controls consistently computed outline-style:none with no box-shadow focus indicator.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a high-contrast :focus-visible outline that is not removed from links, buttons, and search controls.

findings.summary: Consent copy replaces the page purpose in the first viewport
findings.evidence: The page title and underlying content identify the news purpose, but the entire initial viewport is replaced by consent copy and competing consent controls.
findings.suggestedFix: Expose the news hierarchy immediately and move consent into a non-obscuring treatment.

findings.summary: Every core reading flow begins with a blocking detour
findings.evidence: Reading the homepage, opening an article, browsing a section, and viewing search results all begin with the same blocking consent wall, adding a mandatory detour before the core reading flow.
findings.suggestedFix: Allow reading before consent and defer optional vendors until an informed choice.

findings.summary: Largest content is slow
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured LCP 18.3s and performance 0.56; the trace also measured LCP 3.89s and TBT 983.8ms, both showing a poor load under the captured conditions.
findings.suggestedFix: Prioritise the LCP image/content, reduce third-party startup, preload only critical resources, and verify LCP under mobile throttling.

findings.summary: Long tasks block the main thread
findings.evidence: The trace found three long tasks, a 948.6ms longest task, and 983.8ms total blocking time; Lighthouse reported 4.1s main-thread work and 2.2s JS execution.
findings.suggestedFix: Break up or defer ad/analytics work and schedule non-critical tasks by priority.

findings.summary: Resource delivery is heavy and dependency-rich
findings.evidence: The load made 216 requests and transferred 5.64MB; 139 image requests, 8 fonts (798KB), parser-inserted styles/scripts, redirects, and a network dependency warning delay content.
findings.suggestedFix: Shorten critical chains, consolidate fonts/scripts, cache static resources, and defer non-critical delivery.

findings.summary: Duplicate and third-party JavaScript dominates startup
findings.evidence: 29 scripts transferred 1.47MB; multiple GTM/gtag, ad bidding, analytics, and duplicate GPT loads dominate the script inventory and third-party bytes.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove duplicate tag/ad loaders and conditionally load vendors only when needed and consented.

findings.summary: Controls and links lack accessible names
findings.evidence: Lighthouse failed link-name and accessibility-tree audits; the search input has no label or aria-label, and the image audit found five missing alt attributes.
findings.suggestedFix: Label search, name icon links, repair the accessibility tree, and provide meaningful alt text.

findings.summary: Finance values fail minimum contrast
findings.evidence: Lighthouse found market values at 2.5:1 and 4.05:1 against white, below the 4.5:1 minimum for 14px normal text.
findings.suggestedFix: Darken green/red finance text or increase size/weight until measured contrast reaches WCAG minimums.

findings.summary: Heading and focus structure is inconsistent
findings.evidence: The homepage probe found no H1 among its first 30 headings and focused controls had no visible outline; the article gains several consent-system H1s in addition to its article H1.
findings.suggestedFix: Restore one page H1, demote consent headings, and preserve a visible logical focus order.

findings.summary: Browser console errors occur on load
findings.evidence: Lighthouse explicitly failed “Browser errors were logged to the console.”
findings.suggestedFix: Resolve first-party exceptions and isolate vendor failures so a normal load is error-free.

findings.summary: Image markup and formats are inefficient
findings.evidence: The document has doctype and charset, but the image audit found 56 images without srcset, 57 legacy-format images, two missing dimensions, and five missing alt values.
findings.suggestedFix: Add width/height and alt where needed, responsive srcset/sizes, and AVIF/WebP delivery.

findings.summary: Deprecated APIs and BFCache blockers remain
findings.evidence: Lighthouse found a deprecated API, Inspector issues, five BFCache failure reasons, and a missing source-map mapping warning during the run.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove deprecated usage, fix DevTools issues/source maps, and eliminate avoidable BFCache blockers.

findings.summary: Transport defenses and cookie flags are missing
findings.evidence: HTTPS is used, but CSP, HSTS, X-Content-Type-Options, framing protection, Referrer-Policy, and Permissions-Policy are all absent; 16 observed cookies were flagged as not Secure.
findings.suggestedFix: Deploy CSP, HSTS, nosniff, framing protection, Referrer/Permissions policies, and Secure/SameSite cookie attributes.

findings.summary: Third-party data collection is extensive
findings.evidence: The page contacted 31 third-party origins; 156 third-party requests transferred 4.76MB and known Google/DoubleClick trackers plus Yandex/Gemius/ad-tech requests loaded on first visit.
findings.suggestedFix: Inventory vendors, remove redundant trackers, gate optional requests behind consent, and minimise event collection.

findings.summary: Browser-enforced defensive policies are absent
findings.evidence: The response has no HSTS, clickjacking defense, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy, or CSP frame-ancestors fallback.
findings.suggestedFix: Add HSTS, frame-ancestors, Referrer-Policy and a least-privilege Permissions-Policy.

findings.summary: Unknown URLs are misreported as server errors
findings.evidence: A deliberately unknown URL is labeled and rendered as “500 - Sunucu Hatası” rather than a correct 404, making a missing page look like a transient server outage despite offering a home link.
findings.suggestedFix: Return an actual 404 with the existing recovery copy and navigation.

findings.summary: Tracking begins before consent choice
findings.evidence: Tracking and advertising requests are already present in the first-load HAR while the consent wall asks for a decision; the blocking wall obscures content on every sampled route.
findings.suggestedFix: Hold analytics, ad auctions, cookie sync, and non-essential cookies until the user opts in.

findings.summary: Search input disables assistance and lacks a label
findings.evidence: The search input has autocomplete="off" and no associated label or aria-label, obstructing input assistance and accessible identification.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a persistent label/accessible name and use an appropriate autocomplete/search token.

findings.summary: Images are not consistently responsive or modern
findings.evidence: Images transferred 3.25MB across 139 requests; 57 use legacy formats and 56 lack responsive srcset, while Lighthouse estimates 198KiB image savings.
findings.suggestedFix: Generate responsive modern-format variants and choose them with srcset/sizes.

findings.summary: Background advertising and analytics work is wasteful
findings.evidence: The initial page performs 216 requests and 4.1s of main-thread work, including analytics, ad auction, cookie-sync redirects, and background tracking before the user reaches content.
findings.suggestedFix: Deprioritise and batch optional work; stop background fetches when hidden or unconsented.

findings.summary: Third-party budget is disproportionate to the content
findings.evidence: Third parties account for 156 requests and 4.76MB, including multiple ad/analytics stacks; this is disproportionate for a primarily text-and-image news listing.
findings.suggestedFix: Set a vendor/request/byte budget and remove or defer stacks that do not deliver clear reader value.

taskList.title: Stop all optional tracking until consent and replace the blocking consent wall
Remove duplicate vendor loaders and defer third-party startup
Deploy security headers and secure cookie attributes
Repair keyboard focus, accessible names, headings, and contrast
Optimise responsive image and font delivery
Make consent modal semantics correct if modality remains
Return a real 404 for unknown routes
Fix console, deprecated API, source-map, and BFCache issues
Label and assist the search input
Progressively adopt container queries and route transitions
